title: Join Us
text:
We welcome motivated students, postdoctoral researchers, and visiting researchers.
If you are interested in joining the group, please contact Marie at marie.saitou@nmbu.no. Please include:

Why are you interested in our lab? What do you want to learn?
Which paper from the group do you like best, and why?
A brief introduction to you and your research experience, together with your CV.

We may not reply to non-specific enquiries. The University of Göttingen’s dos and don’ts when applying for a PhD position provides useful guidance before writing.

title: Join Us
text:
Funding and study routes


Postdoctoral fellowships
The MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship supports international mobility and can be prepared with NMBU as the host institution. NMBU normally runs an annual proposal masterclass. EMBO also offers international postdoctoral fellowships in the life sciences.
NMBU MSCA Postdoctoral Masterclass · EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships


PhD study at the Faculty of Biosciences
The Biosciences PhD programme includes genomics, biotechnology, basic and applied biology, and related fields. PhD opportunities are normally linked to advertised funded positions.
PhD in Biosciences at NMBU


Master’s study at the Faculty of Biosciences
The Faculty of Biosciences offers master’s education and research projects across the biosciences. The former Genome Sciences programme is no longer admitting new applicants after 2025; prospective students should check the faculty’s current programmes.
Students from partner universities may also be able to join NMBU through Erasmus+ exchange or traineeship routes. Traineeship placements and project supervision depend on faculty and supervisor capacity.
Current programmes at the Faculty of Biosciences · Incoming exchange students and Erasmus+ · Genome Sciences programme notice


Students may also consult the Study in Norway funding information for currently available scholarship and grant routes.
For practical information about degree programmes at the Faculty of Biosciences, PhD procedures, regulations, forms, and master’s thesis documents, see Resources.

title: Join Us
text:
Goals at each career stage
Science is a continuing process of learning and contributing—the PI keeps learning too. Expectations differ by career stage, but all group members should develop increasing independence in asking questions, choosing suitable methods, communicating results, and contributing constructively to the research community. The detailed working principles are described in our Group Expectations.

title: Courses
text:
BIO322 · Advanced Topics in Genomics
How does genome-scale variation generate biological differences between species, among individuals, and between cells? BIO322 connects evolutionary, regulatory, and molecular genomics with computational analysis of real datasets.
The course is organised around genomic evolution between species, variation among individuals, gene regulation within organisms, and a group research proposal. Weekly lectures are combined with group exercises, quizzes, and project work.
10 ECTS · Autumn parallel · English · Campus Ås
Official BIO322 course description

title: Courses
section: BIO326 · Genome Sequencing: Tools and Analysis
text:
BIO326 · Genome Sequencing: Tools and Analysis
BIO326 examines how genome sequences are generated, reconstructed, assessed, and interpreted across eukaryotes, prokaryotes, and microbial communities.
Students combine wet-lab and computational work, including DNA preparation, long-read sequencing, genome assembly, annotation, quality assessment, and analysis of genomic and metagenomic datasets.
10 ECTS · Spring parallel · English · Campus Ås

title: People

Principal investigator




Since 2020




Marie Saitou, PhD

Principal investigator

Marie Saitou established the Saitou Lab at NMBU in 2020. She previously held postdoctoral positions in genetic medicine at the University of Chicago and in evolutionary genomics at the University at Buffalo. She received her PhD in Biological Anthropology from the University of Tokyo in 2017.
Her research combines evolutionary, population, comparative, and functional genomics to study structural variation, gene regulation, adaptation, and the evolution of biological diversity.

Rytis Plioplys

MSc student

Rytis is an MSc student in Genome Science at NMBU. His thesis explores the association between telomere length and epigenetic aging in pregnant women using data from the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study (MoBa).
Co-supervision: Yunsung Lee (Norwegian Institute of Public Health)



AR



From 2026




Abu Rahad

MSc student

Rahad is an MSc student in the European Joint Master’s in Animal Biodiversity and Genomics (EMABG), NMBU–WUR track. His thesis will focus on identifying and prioritizing cattle genes for increased resistance to bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV), integrating CRISPR screening results, single-cell expression data, genetic variation, and CRISPR guide design.
Co-supervision: Victor Boyartchuk (Norwegian University of Life Sciences)

title: Research
text: We study how genomes and biological systems evolve, how genomic variation shapes regulation and traits, and how genomics can inform conservation and breeding.

title: Research
section: 1. Tracing the evolution of genome structure
text:
1. Tracing the evolution of genome structure
We investigate how structural variation, chromosomal rearrangements, and whole-genome duplication arise and shape genome evolution. Atlantic salmon provides a central system for studying the long-term consequences of duplicated genomic regions.
Selected publications

Ancient persistence and recurrent emergence of structural variants across divergent Atlantic salmon lineages
Diblasi et al. · bioRxiv · 2026
Beyond inversions and deletions: the evolutionary and functional insights from translocations, fissions, and fusions in animal genomes

title: Research
section: 2. Linking genomic variation to gene regulation and traits
text:
2. Linking genomic variation to gene regulation and traits
We study how genomic variants alter gene expression, regulatory networks, and phenotypes. This includes regulatory divergence and dosage compensation after whole-genome duplication, as well as genomic responses to domestication and disease.
Selected publications

Imputed graph-genotyped structural variants identify regulatory haplotypes associated with gene expression in Atlantic salmon
Chapis et al. · bioRxiv · 2026
Large-scale eQTL analyses in Atlantic salmon reveal persistent dosage compensation 100 million years after genome duplication
Diblasi et al. · bioRxiv · 2025

title: Research
section: 3. Understanding the evolution of biological systems at the molecular level
text:
3. Understanding the evolution of biological systems at the molecular level
We use comparative genomics and transcriptomics to examine how molecular systems originate and diversify. Current work includes the evolution of vertebrate secretory systems and the trajectory of lactation-related cellular programmes.
Selected publications

Comparative Transcriptomics Suggests that Breast Secretory Epithelium Reuses Gene Repertoires Conserved Across Vertebrates Beyond Mammals

title: Research
section: 4. Applying genomics to conservation and breeding
text:
4. Applying genomics to conservation and breeding
We combine population genomics and evolutionary modelling to understand the condition and vulnerability of wild and managed populations. Applications include hybrid detection in European lobster, threatened aquatic and coastal populations, Atlantic salmon breeding, and the spatial design of marine no-take zones.
